correctness.rationale: The graph is defined by the 24 permutations of length four, so it has exactly six three-pattern vertices and 24 labeled arcs. Every nonnegative unit circulation decomposes into normalized directed simple cycles. For two cycle vertices the minimal common face is the nonnegative-flow face on the union of their arc supports: its affine dimension is |U|-|V(U)|+c(U)-1 because the positive midpoint gives full relative dimension. Hence adjacency is equivalent to cycle rank exactly two. Two exhaustive cycle generators, using minimum vertex and minimum edge respectively, agree on all 160 cyclic edge words. For every one of 12,720 unordered pairs, incidence/DSU rank and an independent contained-cycle count give equivalent adjacency decisions. Integer degree summation gives 2,667 edges and the full cycle-length/degree table. BFS independently checks the diameter and eccentricities. The simple vertices correspond exactly to six-vertex Hamiltonian cycles, since 18 is the affine dimension and exactly their 72 vertices have degree 18. Proof applies only to the stated finite canonical fourth-order polytope; all verification runs on the included actual standalone source.

originality.rationale: The primary full text arXiv:1910.02233 already proves the general cycle-polytope and face-poset description. Those facts and the rank-based edge criterion are explicitly credited, rather than represented as new. The new assertion is the exact computed ten-class degree spectrum, 2,667-edge count, joint cycle-length/degree classification, and 72-vertex Hamiltonian/simple equivalence in the natural unrestricted fourth-order case. The published general face algorithm implies a method of finding the profile, but none of the inspected primary sources states the full evaluated 160-vertex adjacency census or a stronger closed parameter specialization that directly yields the numbers. This originality assessment is conditional on inspected literature; additional unidentified finite tables remain a residual risk.
residual_risks: The general face-poset theorem algorithmically determines this finite profile; the new contribution is the nontrivial complete evaluation, not the known criterion.

value.rationale: The first unrestricted fourth-order frequency polytope has dimension 18 and 160 vertices; the face structure is genuinely more varied than the illustrated low-order model. The complete ten-class degree spectrum is a natural missing local face invariant, not an arbitrarily chosen subset of vertices. It distinguishes precisely 72 geometrically simple Hamiltonian-cycle vertices from 88 nonsimple ones and quantifies the degree dispersion 18 to 159, with the two extreme monotone vertices universal. Exact local adjacency data are useful for navigating extreme attainable consecutive-pattern laws and benchmarking optimization/graph searches on the feasible region, without asserting any unproved general behavior or downstream theorem. This finite self-contained classification is justified by its natural canonical object, exhaustiveness and structural simplicity boundary rather than by novelty or reproducibility alone.
